tasks.title: Finalise the lifecycle command surface and add dune destroy
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 (openspec/changes/sbx-5-sbx-lifecycle-and-doctor) design D1/D2, tasks 1.1-1.3. The sbx-3 backend and sbx-4 egress have landed: internal/dune/runtime/sbx/{backend.go,lifecycle.go,egress.go,validate.go,policy_log.go,runner.go} with the D5 runner seam (Runner.Capture/Stream, fakeRunner in runner_test.go). app.go already wires up = Validate -> Ensure -> VerifyEgressPosture -> Status -> Start (if !Running) -> Shell (runUp, internal/dune/app.go:170-191); down = Validate -> Stop; rebuild = Validate -> Rebuild, where Rebuild recreates via `sbx rm --force` -> Ensure -> VerifyEgressPosture -> Start (lifecycle.go:106-129). So 1.1/1.2 are largely realised; this lap FINALISES the contract and ADDS the first-class `dune destroy` verb (D2), resolving the sbx-3 deferred removal question.

Outcome: a new `dune destroy` command that removes the instance's sandbox via `sbx rm` (the `sbx rm --force` shape is already used by Rebuild at lifecycle.go:115; `--force` is required when stdin is not a TTY per design D1) and REQUIRES confirmation or an explicit `--force` flag, NEVER deleting the profile-scoped persist dir (the XDG persist location from ensureProfilePersistDir, lifecycle.go:271). `down` stays stop-only; confirm `up` reuses a running sandbox without recreation and `rebuild` preserves profile-scoped persisted state.

Files & scope: add CommandDestroy + a `--force` flag to internal/dune/cli/options.go (mirror parseContainerCommand); add a backend Destroy/Remove method in the sbx package constructing `sbx rm --force <instance>` through the runner seam (or reuse the shape Rebuild uses); wire it into dispatchRuntimeCommand (internal/dune/app.go:141) with a confirmation prompt (or --force); update helpText. NOTE: dune.Run currently threads no stdin (cmd/dune/main.go:12 passes only os.Stdout/os.Stderr) — an interactive prompt needs stdin threaded into Run/dispatch, or default to requiring --force. Do NOT add dune ports (next lap), the dune logs recomposition, diagnostics, or doctor here.

Design: reconfirm `sbx rm --help` before pinning (multiple-name args + `--force` for non-TTY, design D1). The confirmation UX (interactive prompt vs --force) is the design's open question; whatever the wording, BOTH paths must be tested. Keep concrete sbx command shapes private to the sbx package (backend.go convention).

Acceptance: fakeRunner tests pin the `sbx rm --force <instance>` vector for destroy and assert the up/down/rebuild sequencing (reuse-running on up, stop-only down, rebuild recreate-preserving-persist) — task 5.1. A test confirms destroy WITHOUT confirmation and WITHOUT --force does not construct `sbx rm`, and that destroy never targets the persist dir. `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green. Report the exact destroy confirmation/force behavior.

tasks.title: Add dune ports over the verified sbx ports surface
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 design D1, task 1.4. A new first-class `dune ports` verb wrapping the `sbx ports` surface. Spike 4 confirmed the shapes: list `sbx ports <sandbox>` (+ `--json`); publish `sbx ports <sandbox> --publish [[HOST_IP:]HOST_PORT:]SANDBOX_PORT[/PROTOCOL]` (ephemeral host port when HOST_PORT omitted, loopback bind when HOST_IP omitted); unpublish `sbx ports <sandbox> --unpublish [HOST_IP:]HOST_PORT:SANDBOX_PORT[/PROTOCOL]` (repeatable). Goes through the sbx-3 D5 runner seam so argument construction is fakeRunner-assertable (design D1). Builds on the lifecycle lap; reuses the same seam.

Outcome: backend Ports methods (sbx package) for list/publish/unpublish built on the verified shapes, plus `dune ports` CLI wiring that SURFACES the loopback-vs-all-interfaces caveat: a nested service bound only to sandbox loopback may not be reachable via a published host port, so dev servers should bind to all sandbox interfaces when host exposure is wanted (spike 2).

Files & scope: add CommandPorts + a ports arg/flag parse to internal/dune/cli/options.go (list is the default; --publish/--unpublish take a port spec); add list/publish/unpublish methods in the sbx package via the runner seam; wire into dispatchRuntimeCommand (internal/dune/app.go); update helpText. Do not add diagnostics/doctor or the dune logs recomposition.

Design: reconfirm `sbx ports --help` before pinning (especially the `--unpublish` spelling). Use the per-command JSON flag (`sbx ports <sandbox> --json`) if parsing the list; do NOT assume a uniform `--json` across sbx verbs (design D1 / sbx-3 D6). Validate any user-supplied port spec so it cannot reshape the constructed invocation (mirror validateSecretService in secrets.go).

Acceptance: fakeRunner tests pin the list (`sbx ports <instance>` [+ `--json`]), publish (`--publish <spec>`), and unpublish (`--unpublish <spec>`) vectors; a test exercises the loopback-vs-all-interfaces guidance on a publish attempt (spec scenario). `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Recompose dune logs from Dune-owned logs and sbx policy log
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 design D3, tasks 2.1-2.2. The interim Logs (lifecycle.go:90) currently runs `sbx exec <instance> bash -lc <script>` to tail /var/log/dune/*.log with an optional service arg (logsScript, lifecycle.go:321). PolicyLog (policy_log.go:47) already wraps `sbx policy log <instance> --json --limit <n>` into PolicyLogReport{BlockedHosts,AllowedHosts}. sbx-4 removed Pipelock entirely — there is no `dune logs pipelock`. This lap COMPOSES the final `dune logs`.

Outcome: `dune logs` composes (a) Dune-owned setup/runtime logs from TWO pinned sources — the host-side lifecycle log the runner writes for sandbox create/start/attach diagnostics, PLUS the in-sandbox /var/log/dune/ output (the sbx-2 D5a contract, e.g. the re-homed setup-persist.log) read via `sbx exec` — and (b) `sbx policy log <instance>` egress records (reusing the existing PolicyLog). This RESOLVES design D3 / the open question on the Dune-owned source by picking it and ASSERTING both Dune-owned sources appear in the composed output. No `dune logs pipelock` surface (already gone). App-dependency service logs are NOT aggregated here (project-owned Compose -> `docker compose logs` inside the sandbox).

Files & scope: the sbx package (compose the host-side log + the existing /var/log/dune tail + PolicyLog into the logs path) and the app.go logs dispatch. If no host-side lifecycle log exists yet, add a minimal durable one written through/alongside the runner seam (D3 says "the host-side log the lifecycle commands already write" — establish it if absent). Keep `dune logs` arg parsing back-compatible (the interim service arg). Do not add diagnostics/doctor.

Design: D3 leaves the exact host-side source to implementation — choose the smallest durable source and pin its presence in tests rather than leaving it an open question. Reuse the existing PolicyLog rather than re-shelling `sbx policy log`; its JSON field names are already pinned in policy_log.go — keep that. Keep concrete sbx shapes in the sbx package.

Acceptance: a test asserts the composed `dune logs` output includes BOTH a Dune-owned log line (host-side and/or /var/log/dune) AND `sbx policy log` records, and that no `pipelock` subcommand exists (spec scenario). `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Add structured sbx diagnostics with stable codes
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 design D4, tasks 3.1-3.3 and 5.2. Today every sbx backend method returns a plain fmt.Errorf wrap (lifecycle.go create/start/stop/rm, validate.go diagnose/version, egress.go allow/deny/rm, secrets.go). D4 introduces a small, sbx-scoped DiagnosticError {Code, Summary, Detail, Cause, Command, Stderr, Recovery} with IsDiagnostic/AsDiagnostic and WrapCommandError(code, summary, result, err) — reusing the superseded ref-3 shape, retargeted to sbx.

Outcome: the DiagnosticError type + helpers, and backend failures MAPPED to the initial small code set: sbx.not_installed, sbx.diagnose_failed, sbx.version_below_min, sbx.create_failed, sbx.start_failed, sbx.stop_failed, sbx.exec_failed, sbx.rm_failed, template.unavailable, policy.apply_failed, workspace.invalid, profile.config_corrupt. The failing command's stderr is PRESERVED (the default runner already attaches output to ExitError.Stderr, runner.go:30) rather than replaced with friendly prose; recovery hints attach for common host/setup failures; the original cause stays errors.Is/As-unwrap-compatible. Default CLI output is concise (summary + recovery); full command/stderr shows only under a verbose mode.

Files & scope: a diagnostics file in the sbx package (or a small sub-package) for the type/helpers; convert the EXISTING and the newly-added (destroy/ports/logs) backend methods to emit coded diagnostics at the boundary where context is known; thread a verbose toggle into CLI rendering (app.go). If WrapCommandError needs the command vector + stderr + exit, extend the runner seam minimally to surface a CommandResult. Do not add doctor (next lap) — but design the codes/hints so doctor can reuse them.

Design: keep the taxonomy SMALL — add a code only when Dune can actually distinguish the case (design risk: taxonomy sprawl). Map at the boundary; do not double-wrap. Tests assert codes and key fields, NOT rendered prose.

Acceptance: tests assert codes + preserved stderr for representative failures (missing sbx, failed diagnose, below-min version, create/start/exec/rm failures, template unavailable, corrupt profiles) — task 5.2; plus a concise-vs-verbose rendering test. `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Add the read-only dune doctor readiness command
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 design D5, tasks 4.1-4.3 and 5.3. `dune doctor` reports readiness WITHOUT creating, starting, or entering a sandbox, reusing the superseded ref-4 Check model {ID, Group, Severity, Status, Summary, Detail, Recovery} with Status pass|warn|fail|skip, and reusing the D4 diagnostic codes/recovery hints (prior lap) where a check maps to a runtime failure mode.

Outcome: a `dune doctor` command (+ --verbose, optional --json) whose check groups each use ONLY read-only sbx calls: host/sbx (sbx on PATH; `sbx diagnose --output json` — the validate.go form, NOT `--json`; min version via `sbx version` >= minimumSbxVersion v0.32.0); template (version.SbxTemplateRef() known and available — lightweight, no forced full pull by default; deep mode opt-in, flag name still open); sandbox (status via `sbx ls --json`, REUSING the sbx-3 D7 parseSandboxList/Status path, not a second parser); workspace/profile/config (workspace.Resolve + slug; profiles.json parses or is safely absent; effective profile valid; config/data/persist dirs readable/writable/creatable); egress (posture non-Open and inspectable via `sbx policy ls` — reuse inspectEgressPosture/classifyEgressPosture from egress.go; WARN when unconfirmable, FAIL only on an observed Open posture, per sbx-4 D1; never mutate policy). No in-template service-health checks.

Files & scope: a doctor file/sub-package (the Check model + a runner) + CommandDoctor in internal/dune/cli/options.go + dispatch wiring in internal/dune/app.go + helpText. Reuse existing readiness primitives (Validate internals, the Status parse, the egress inspection) rather than duplicating sbx shapes. Output concise human-readable by default; `--json` emits the structured check list.

Design: doctor MUST be non-mutating — it MUST NOT construct `sbx create`/`run`/`exec`/`rm`; assert this in tests. Keep template availability lightweight (deep checks opt-in) to control cost. Reuse the D4 codes/hints where a check corresponds to a runtime failure mode. Doctor reports readiness; it does not guarantee the environment works (smoke still required).

Acceptance: tests cover pass/warn/fail/skip cases and the `--json` shape, and ASSERT doctor constructs only read-only sbx calls (diagnose/version/ls/policy ls) and never a sandbox-mutating command — task 5.3. `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Smoke-verify the finalised commands against the dune-sbx template
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 task 6.2 + design Migration plan, "Smoke verification against the sbx binary" — the empirical acceptance gates against a real installed `sbx` and the Dune sbx template (ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx, version from container/sbx/IMAGE_VERSION), mirroring the sbx-3 and sbx-4 smoke laps. Requires `sbx` authenticated on the host.

Outcome: in an ephemeral instance, capture and record: (a) `dune destroy --force` removes the sandbox (absent from `sbx ls --json`), and a subsequent `dune up` RECREATES it with profile-scoped persisted state intact (ties to the sbx-3 D3 persist sentinel); (b) `dune doctor` is NON-mutating — running it against an absent and a stopped sandbox does not change what `sbx ls --json` reports (no create/start), and on a healthy host the host/sbx and sandbox checks report pass; (c) `dune logs` surfaces both a Dune-owned line and `sbx policy log` records for a running instance, and exposes no `pipelock` subcommand; (d) `dune ports` lists via `sbx ports <sandbox>` and the loopback-vs-all-interfaces guidance is exercised on a publish attempt.

Files & scope: a smoke harness/justfile recipe consistent with the existing smoke approach; may shell out to the real `sbx`; build an ephemeral container to test in if needed (permitted by AGENTS.md). Remove ALL temporary sandboxes (`sbx rm`) at the end (task 6.2).

Design: keep the gate honest — if `sbx`/the template are unavailable in this environment, report that explicitly rather than faking a pass; never weaken egress to Open to make a check pass.

Acceptance: the four observations above captured with the actual commands/output; `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./...` green; temp sandboxes removed. Report the recorded evidence for the docs lap.

tasks.title: Document the finalised command surface, logs, diagnostics, and doctor
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-5 task 6.3. Update the same docs surface sbx-3/sbx-4 touched (README + docs/architecture), matching the existing tone/structure.

Outcome: docs describe (1) the finalised dune verbs on sbx — up/down/destroy/rebuild/logs/ports — including that `dune destroy` removes the sandbox (`sbx rm`) while profile-scoped persisted state survives, and the `dune ports` loopback-vs-all-interfaces caveat; (2) the `dune logs` composition (Dune-owned setup/runtime logs + `sbx policy log`), that `dune logs pipelock` is gone, and that app-dependency service logs come from `docker compose logs` inside the sandbox (project-owned Compose); (3) the structured diagnostics (stable codes, preserved stderr, recovery hints, concise vs verbose); (4) `dune doctor` — read-only readiness, the check groups, and `--json`. Fold in any guidance the smoke lap recorded.

Files & scope: README and docs/architecture (e.g. the host-cli / lifecycle doc); do not edit openspec change files as docs. No code changes.

Acceptance: docs render cleanly and a reader can find how to destroy/rebuild safely, where `dune logs` reads from, and what `dune doctor` checks; the pipelock-is-gone and docker-compose-logs notes are present.
